title: Etale invariance of the pointwise complete-intersection condition over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $Y$ and $Z$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $e:Z\to Y$ be an etale $k$-morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every point $z\in Z$, writing $y=e(z)$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$ if and only if $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$, in the local-ring meaning fixed by [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion]. No surjectivity, quasi-compactness, separation or perfection assumption on $k$ is imposed; empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tag 036S (lemma-syntomic-syntomic-local-source), applied to structural morphisms over a field and to the open image of an etale neighbourhood; pointwise interpretation in morphisms.tex Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic).

proof.text: Write $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structural map, for $T=Y,Z$. Each stalk is a $k$-vector space, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so $a_T$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The spectrum of a field is locally Noetherian: its one affine chart has coordinate ring $k$, whose only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; use [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Local finite type and [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] therefore give local finite presentation of both $a_T$.

source.place: Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic), flatness and finite-presentation hypotheses over a field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change] to $a_Y$ and $a_Z$, obtaining open loci $L_Y,L_Z$. The unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has residue field $k$; by [def-pc-scheme-fibre], its fibre is $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong T$, with the structural $k$-action unchanged (the inverse sends $t$ to $(t,a_T(t))$). Thus $t\in L_T$ exactly when $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is CI over $k$. The cited locus theorem also says that $L_T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is syntomic in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-syntomic-etale-source-locality], and every source open on which $a_T$ is syntomic is contained in $L_T$.

Suppose $y=e(z)\in L_Y$, and put $U=e^{-1}(L_Y)$, which contains $z$. The restricted map $U\to L_Y$ is etale: the inclusions $U\to Z$ and $L_Y\to Y$ are open immersions and hence etale; compose $U\to Z\to Y$, then cancel $L_Y\to Y$ using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Part (1) of [lem-sfb-syntomic-etale-source-locality] applied to $L_Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ syntomic. Maximality of $L_Z$ from step 2 gives $z\in U\subseteq L_Z$.

Conversely let $z\in L_Z$, put $W=L_Z$, and set $V=e(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], $V$ is an open neighbourhood of $y$. The map $W\to V$ is surjective by the definition of $V$ and etale by the same open-immersion composition and cancellation as in step 3, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The composite $W\to V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is syntomic by step 2. Apply part (2) of [lem-sfb-syntomic-etale-source-locality] to the singleton cover $W\to V$: $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is syntomic. Maximality in step 2 yields $y\in V\subseteq L_Y$, proving the reverse implication. If $Z$ is empty there are no points to check; nothing requires $e$ to cover $Y$.
